title: Clean-Architecture Layer Bloat (CRUD Over-Structuring)
pattern: Splitting a basic CRUD data operation into 6+ distinct physical files and abstract adapter interfaces (Controller, Presenter, Interactor, Repository, DBModel, DomainEntity) in a simple startup application.
why_bad: Severe developer exhaustion and extreme development friction. Adding a single field (like a user's nickname) requires modifying 6 files and writing extensive mapping boilerplate, grinding development velocity to a halt for zero architectural gain.
detection: Look for a design containing more than 5 distinct, sequential mapping layers for standard database reads and writes with no rich domain logic.
counterexample: Highly complex business domains with extensive, volatile business rules where strict interactor isolation is necessary to protect core invariants.
fix: Simplify. For simple CRUD, let your handler fetch the record directly from a repository, only adding complex interactors where the domain rules are genuinely rich.
source: *Robert C. Martin - Clean Architecture (2017)*; *Titus Winters et al. - Software Engineering at Google (2020)*, Chapter 14.
